ethiopian-empire.framingNotes: “It existed from around 1137 to 1947…” / “The Zagwe Dynasty was later overthrown… in 1270.” Ethiopia is framed as a long-lasting Christian empire defined by dynastic continuity and resilience against external threats.
ethiopian-empire.analystNotes: The establishment of the Solomonic Dynasty in 1270 falls directly within the 13th century, making this a direct reference point. The text presents Ethiopia as a continuous imperial structure entering the 13th century through dynastic transition.

topicsPresent: Decline through invasion, rebellion, and environmental change
ghana-empire.framingNotes: “This was a kingdom that lasted from the 6th to the 13th Century.” / “In 1203, Kumbi Saleh was attacked…” Ghana is framed as a trade empire whose decline culminates in the 13th century.
ghana-empire.analystNotes: Direct reference to 1203 and explicit statement of existence into the 13th century make this directly relevant. The narrative emphasises collapse at the start of the 13th century.

topicsPresent: Economic system based on gold and trade
mali-empire.framingNotes: “This was an Empire in West Africa which existed from 1230 to 1670.” Mali is framed as a powerful Islamic trading empire with strong leadership and administrative organisation.
mali-empire.analystNotes: The foundation (1230) and early rule (1255) fall squarely in the 13th century. Direct coverage of formation phase.

song-china.framingNotes: “Chinese history of civilisation began around 1500 BC…” China is presented as a continuous civilisation focused on early dynasties and achievements.
song-china.analystNotes: Song China existed in the 13th century but is not explicitly mentioned. Structural features (state, trade, technology) provide indirect relevance.

inca-empire.framingNotes: “...settled in the valley near Cusco Circa in 1200…” Inca are framed as a highly organised empire with strong infrastructure and social systems.
inca-empire.analystNotes: The origin around 1200 places the Inca in early 13th century context, but most content focuses on later development. Indirect relevance through formation.
